c.tagline: The world's smallest state, home to the Pope and the greatest art on Earth.

taxi.fareNote: No taxis or ride-hail pick up inside the Vatican walls; use licensed white Rome taxis from the ranks at Piazza del Risorgimento or the edge of St. Peter's Square, or Rome's Free Now / Uber. Fixed fares apply from Rome's airports (about €55 from Fiumicino).

emergency.note: Within the enclave the Vatican Gendarmerie polices the state; for emergencies dial Rome's 112 (police) or 118 (ambulance), or the EU-wide 112.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the crowds in St Peter's Square and museum queues; ignore unofficial 'skip-the-line' ticket touts on the approach streets.

hood_desc: The largest church in the world and the spiritual centre of Roman Catholicism, built over the tomb of St. Peter and topped by Michelangelo's dome; inside are Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's bronze baldachin, and you can climb the cupola for sweeping views over Rome.

A roughly 7-kilometre sequence of galleries holding one of the world's greatest art collections — the Raphael Rooms, the Gallery of Maps, Egyptian and classical antiquities — leading ultimately to the Sistine Chapel; queues are long, so book a timed ticket ahead.

The atmospheric medieval quarter between the Vatican and Castel Sant'Angelo, threaded by grand Via della Conciliazione and narrow lanes of trattorias, guesthouses and souvenir shops; together with neighbouring Prati it is where most visitors actually stay and eat.
lodging: The Spring House Hotel Rome Vatican

water.note: Tap and fountain water is safe and excellent, as throughout Rome.

transit.hours: Rome's Metro Line A runs about 5:30am-11:30pm (until 1:30am Fri-Sat); night buses cover the network afterwards. Everything within the Vatican itself is reached on foot.
transit.note: The only rail inside the walls is the ceremonial Vatican railway station, which has no scheduled passenger service.
transit.pay: Vatican City has no transit system of its own; you ride Rome's ATAC network. Buy a BIT ticket (€1.50/$1.60, valid 100 minutes) from tobacco shops or machines, or tap a contactless card at metro gates. Line A stops Ottaviano-San Pietro and Cipro sit just outside the walls, a short walk from St. Peter's and the Vatican Museums.

transit.m: Leonardo Express to Termini, then Metro A to Ottaviano (~50 min)
FL1 regional train to Roma San Pietro (~45 min)
Taxi (fixed €55 fare from FCO to central Rome)

tip.r: Service (servizio) or a cover charge (coperto) is often included; round up or leave a euro or two for good service.

landmarks: St. Peter's Basilica
The largest and most important church in Christendom, crowned by Michelangelo's soaring dome and filled with masterpieces like the Pietà.
St. Peter's Square
Bernini's monumental elliptical piazza, framed by curving colonnades of 284 columns, is the grand welcoming stage for papal audiences.
Sistine Chapel
Home to Michelangelo's breathtaking ceiling and Last Judgment fresco, this is the single most famous ceiling in art history.
Vatican Museums
An immense complex of galleries housing centuries of papal art collections, culminating in the world-renowned Sistine Chapel.
Vatican Gardens
Manicured lawns, fountains, and woodland covering half of Vatican City offer a tranquil, photogenic escape behind the basilica.
Apostolic Palace
The Pope's official residence and workplace, visible from St. Peter's Square, symbolizes the seat of papal authority.
Baldachin of St. Peter (Bernini's Baldacchino)
A towering bronze canopy by Bernini rising over the papal altar, an unmissable Baroque masterpiece inside the basilica.
Vatican Necropolis (Tomb of St. Peter)
An ancient underground burial ground believed to hold the tomb of St. Peter himself, reachable via a special guided excavation tour.
Raphael Rooms (Stanze di Raffaello)
A suite of papal reception rooms frescoed by Raphael, including the iconic 'School of Athens,' rivaling the Sistine Chapel for artistic wonder.
Vatican Obelisk
A 4,000-year-old Egyptian obelisk standing at the center of St. Peter's Square, the only obelisk in Rome that has stood since ancient Roman times.

train.note: The Vatican has its own station, Città del Vaticano, but no scheduled passenger service - it is used for freight and the occasional papal or excursion train. In practice you use Rome's network: Roma Termini and Roma San Pietro are both a short ride away on Trenitalia (https://www.trenitalia.com), with metro line A to Ottaviano the usual approach on foot.

bus.note: There are no coach routes from the Vatican itself - the whole state is half a square kilometre. Rome's ATAC buses and trams stop right outside the walls at Piazza Risorgimento and along Via di Porta Cavalleggeri, and long-distance coaches use Roma Tiburtina, about 20 minutes away by metro.

ferry.note: The Vatican is landlocked inside Rome with no river frontage of its own, so there are no ferries. Rome's Tiber sightseeing boats and the port at Civitavecchia, about 80 km away, are the nearest water transport.

half.name: Colosseum and Roman Forum
half.blurb: The Colosseum and Roman Forum are ancient Rome's core ruins, a short distance from Vatican City across the Tiber.

half.name: Trevi Fountain and Pantheon
half.blurb: The Trevi Fountain and Pantheon sit in central Rome's historic core, an easy walk or bus ride from the Vatican.

half.name: Ostia Antica
half.blurb: Ostia Antica is the excavated ruin of ancient Rome's main seaport, with a preserved theater, baths and mosaic floors.

half.name: Tivoli
half.blurb: Tivoli has two UNESCO sites: Villa d'Este's terraced fountain gardens and the sprawling ruins of Emperor Hadrian's villa complex.
